env.note: Supplementary analyses rc3, rc4, rc6, rc9

binary_corpora_dis_determinism.claim: For binary-label corpora (MultiPICo, EPIC), dis_i = H(p_ironic) / log(k_i) is a deterministic function of (p_ironic, k_i). When k_i is fixed, dis_i is a monotone function of |p_ironic - 0.5|.

MultiPICo.interpretation: dis_i is NOT mean-independent in the same sense as CSC relative variance; it IS a function of p_ironic. Mean-independence claim is valid only for CSC (Likert).

CSC_mean_independence.interpretation: CSC: Spearman(dis, mean_eval) should be near 0 if mean-independent. Relative variance with floor is approximately mean-independent but not perfectly so.

MHS_dis_vs_mean.interpretation: MHS: dis_i = H(p_hate)/log(2) is monotone in |p_hate - 0.5|. The claim of mean-independence applies only to CSC (Likert scale).

CSC_correct_dis_mi.interpretation: CSC dis_mi is approximately mean-independent (rho_dis_mean ~ 0.07 after correct normalization). Denominator floor at 0.5 applied to ~8% of items.

MultiPICo_EPIC_correct.note: Paper Eq.2 writes denominator as log(K_i) but code normalizes by log(2) (= 1 for binary entropy in bits). For binary labels these are equivalent when K_i=2; for K_i>2, H_bits(p) <= 1 always since there are only 2 outcomes.
MultiPICo_EPIC_correct.interpretation: For binary corpora, dis_mi = H_bits(p_ironic) is a MONOTONE SYMMETRIC function of |p_ironic - 0.5|. This is NOT mean-independent: items with p_ironic near 0.5 always have high dis regardless of the mean. Mean-independence claim (CSC §) is valid only for CSC Likert scale.

MHS.interpretation: MHS dis is also H_bits(p_hate), monotone in |p_hate-0.5|. Not mean-independent.

summary_Eq1.paper_claim_mean_independent: Valid for CSC only; binary corpora have dis = f(p) which is symmetric but NOT mean-independent in general
